events.name: Akosombo/Kpong Dam spillage (Lower Volta)
events.method: Sentinel-1 RTC (calibrated gamma0) VV change detection: >|3|dB drop baseline->peak, pre-existing water excluded (adaptive: max of -17 dB and the baseline's 8th percentile), blobs <8px removed. Rain-wetted soil also darkens VV -- read margins as indicative, not a surveyed flood line.

events.name: Weija Dam spillage #2 (Tetegu / Weija Gbawe, Sept 2026)
events.method: Sentinel-1 RTC (calibrated gamma0) VV change detection: >|3|dB drop baseline->peak, pre-existing water excluded (adaptive: max of -17 dB and the baseline's 8th percentile), blobs <8px removed. Rain-wetted soil also darkens VV -- read margins as indicative, not a surveyed flood line.
events.known_limitation: Detected 0.0 km2 -- almost certainly a FALSE NEGATIVE, not evidence against the news-confirmed flooding (submerged homes/roads in Tetegu/Oblogo/Weija, residents evacuating by canoe). The same-orbit revisit gap left a 4-day hole after the spillage (2026-09-09): no ascending pass exists on 09-10/11/12, unlike the May event where the peak scene landed the very next day. The May event itself showed this flooding recedes fast (5.0 km2 new flood -> 1.3 km2 still flooded within 12 days), so a flashy flood here plausibly receded before the first available same-orbit pass. A diagnostic orbit-mismatched comparison (ascending baseline vs. the 09-14 descending scene) found 0.35 km2, but a ~1.5 dB systematic shift between the two orbits' medians makes that number unreliable, not a confirmed smaller re-measurement. Net: this is a satellite-revisit coverage gap, not a sign the flood didn't happen or was smaller than May's.

events.method: Sentinel-1 RTC (calibrated gamma0) VV change detection: >|3|dB drop baseline->peak, pre-existing water excluded (adaptive: max of -17 dB and the baseline's 8th percentile), blobs <8px removed. Rain-wetted soil also darkens VV -- read margins as indicative, not a surveyed flood line.
events.known_limitation: No exact day is documented for this event (only "March 2017"), and no end date is documented either -- Daily Graphic (Jun 27 2017) confirms flooding was STILL ongoing 3 months in. 'peak' and 'recession' here are therefore both just points within an undocumented-length sustained flood, not a true peak-to-recession bracket like the day-dated Weija events.
